visual_text: Normal bowel frequency covers a wide range
Once a day is the most common pattern, but not the only one
Bristol study: a regular daily cycle in 40 in 100 men and 33 in 100 women.
96 in 100 US adults who called their bowels normal, and 98 in 100 healthy Swedish adults aged 18 to 70, fell in this range
Heaton, Gut, 1992; Mitsuhashi, Am J Gastroenterol, 2018; Walter, Scand J Gastroenterol, 2010
Constipation: hard or lumpy stools, straining, a feeling of not having emptied, or fewer than 3 a week, a good part of the time.
Tell your GP about a change from your usual pattern that lasts
Tell your GP about blood from the back passage or in the stool
Tell your GP about weight loss you can't explain
Chang, Gastroenterology, 2023; Monahan, Gut, 2022; Assmann, United European Gastroenterol J, 2022
alt_text: Chart and scale. Bristol study: a regular daily bowel cycle in 40 in 100 men and 33 in 100 women. A wide band from 3 times a day to 3 times a week held 96 in 100 US adults reporting normal bowels and 98 in 100 healthy Swedish adults. Arrows mark more often and less often.

Text card. Constipation means hard or lumpy stools, straining, feeling not emptied, or fewer than 3 a week, a good part of the time. Three numbered points: tell your GP about a lasting change, blood from the back passage or in the stool, or unexplained weight loss.
design_instructions: 2-card carousel. Card 1: headline, kicker, Bristol bars 40 and 33 of 100 (C12-25-a), scale band between 3 times a day and 3 times a week with end labels, more/less often, 96/98 in 100 statement (C12-25-c). Card 2: definition and mint panel with three numbered GP items.
